UPDATE -- The issues I reported below have been fixed or much improved. Thank you!! ---- Excellent syncing to Google Drive, no sync errors encountered yet. I can write on the same story from either tablet or phone whenever I want, without messing with trading files around. 5 stars for that!! REQUESTS/BUGFIXES -- Support volume up/down buttons for scrolling in both edit and preview modes. ----- It's near-impossible to scroll through a file in edit mode on a phone. In dark theme night vision the scrollbar is invisible, and tapping anywhere on screen moves the cursor there and opens the software keyboard. If you manage to very carefully scroll down a few screens'-worth, the slightest wrong tap jerks you back to the last location of the cursor and opens the keyboard again. -- Move cursor to somewhere in current displayed screen when scrolling in edit mode. ---- I hate getting jerked back to the previous location of the cursor. The text I am looking at is the text I want to edit next, so I would love it if the cursor moves with me. -- Keep same location in file when switching between preview and edit modes. ---- I preview a file to read through it. When I see something to fix I switch to edit mode, but I'm jerked back to the last location of the edit mode cursor and can't get to the location I was previewing. Same when I want to read through something I've written, I switch to preview mode, but then I have to scroll down from the top of the file to wherever I was editing. -- Fix weird bug where cursor gets misaligned to text when syntax highlighting changes the line heights. ---- Tapping on a screen containing ** or # styles applies italic or bold formatting to that text, but also rerenders the text with different line heights. The cursor doesn't know these new line heights, so it drifts out of alignment and you have to guess which line it thinks it's in. (This occurs with Ideal Sans font, 1.15x line height. I didn't test with other appearance settings.)
Clean, easy to use and understand, and perfect for writing a quick, on-the-go note. I would maybe like to see support for other file types besides ".txt", as well as more formatting options.

Intuitive, Clever Features! I write while out and about, all day long, and have tried a few other programs but this one offers everything an author could want! (I purchased the $5 package) Pros: ---This app has struck a harmonious balance between customization and minimalism. You're able to make a few key changes to appearance settings without scrolling endlessly through options. ---Jottpad has some unique features that are so helpful for an author, you can tell the developers had insight when making this. The extended keyboard offers simple arrow keys that allow you to move the cursor one space at a time rather than tap a word 10 times trying to get it to the right spot. ---Another great feature is the Typewriter! Omg I didn't realize the awesomeness of this right away, but it's done wonders! Typewriter mode dulls everything except the 2 previous lines you've written. Super great for keeping from getting distracted!! No scrolling, no distraction, just write! Cons: ---To be honest, the only negative I've found so far is regarding exports. You have to exp as .txt otherwise it compiles everything as a massive chunk of text :/ no bueno. Tried the .docx export but it wouldn't work for me (still in beta tho; if they get that up and running then this'd be a non-issue!) ---I also couldn't view any of my Google docs. All my folders were visible but opening them showed "no files found". I can create a new file and find it in gdocs later, but can't view an already created document. All in all, a simple and intuitive app for writing that I definitely recommend! Great job, developers!!!

I'm also a bit surprised that something other apps offer for free easily, Night Mode, is locked off behind a pay wall. I feel if the app could be optimized a bit, it might speed things up. Edit: I find it interesting that the developers of jotterpad decided to advertise to me about all the features their product has instead of actually answering my concerns about the app's performance issues. Also, if you're writting in down time in a busy day (the sort of situations these types of apps were made for) it can become annoying as when you put your phone to sleep and pick it up some seconds later it scrolls all the way up to the top of the page. This wouldn't be a problem per se if you're writting a poem or something obviously, but when even writting short stories (especially the ones that quickly no longer can be called short) it can be bothersome. This is added to by the fact thst this app isn't very kind to your battery life; some apps have been worse, but this is still pretty bad. Book Writer Free (the one with the purple pencil logo) is better in these regards, as it's more battery friendly, it doesn't scroll you to the top as much (still does it occasionally) but even when it does, BWF allows you to separate chapters in each story making the scroll back MUCH more tolerable. If this app can do more with less battery power, why is this one such a power chomper? The font also is clearly made for small screens in this app, not bad neccesarily, but you would have to do more scrolling than others. Jotterpad also has sparse options for punctuation or alternate font types, and the few it does have don't work 99% of the time. Screenwriting: Good, but needs improvement For a long time i was looking to write hassle free way of writing screenplays on my android tablet, so i can completely do away with the laptop. I think JotterPad enables me to do so. First is "fountain", the syntax is so simplified and unlike clunky celtx app, it is so easy to write a screenplay and even take out pdf print. Problem is there is no good documentation or video to explain, what syntax to use for screenplays. It took me while to figure out, but after that it was very reliable specially compared to Celtx. But there is lot of scope of improvement. Second is dropbox integration on phone. While on my tablet it is perfect. Somehow my phone the dropbox folder don't show up the file structure. I have found a way around. But considering i have paid for app and it should be simple and not a workaround. Third, support is bad. I am paid customer and i get reply after two days, with a line "plz try to reinstall", of course do you think i am fool, If i can discover workaround, it means i have already reinstalled. But i still see hope because after celtx, myscreenplay, this is better way to write screenplay on android. Developers should allow users to try out screenplay feature before they buy. I was not very sure. i took a gamble. Despite flaws, I see myself using it for long period of time, unless better app comes up or developers loose interest in the app development. P. The developers helped me install this custom font (as I had originally put it in the wrong place). And, after I requested a larger maximum font size setting (for eyesight and also for Chinese characters), they replied and told me that this adjustment would be coming soon (in the beta). I'll wait patiently for this final detail to be released. 3. It is minimalist but strikes the perfect balance for me. So I hope you stop asking for more features. :-) EDIT: I learned how to use (accessibility) zoom and pan, but I still hope to see the larger font size setting mentioned above.

The big advantage with this notepad app on many others, is that it puts all your notes in txt files in the folder of your choice, so that you can back them up and do exactly what you want with them. They're proprely yours, they dont hang somewhere in the skies. Better still, if you already have some notes in txt format, you just have to tell the app where they are, by driving through the folder's path (up left on the home screen) and it will nicely open and list them for you. Another thing is that it's very sleek and neat. There's no lag and no jumpy scrolling and no cheap or poor operation about it. Evereything you do comes smooth and cool on the eye. There are not many settings and fancy business, and not a lot to customize, but it does it simply and very well. Undo redo, a discreet slider on the right for long files, a search tool, the app remembers your last position. If like me you're not Shakespeare and just need a clean notepad to jot down a few thoughts, this one might answer your need. The only thing I'm missing is the ability to change the background color on the fly, as in Google Keep, so that when the surrounding light goes down you can apply a light-blue or a dark-blue background to suit your eyes. I find it much more convenient than a night theme meant to work in the dark. I hope these color backgrounds will come along. I have the Paid version (Creative) since last year, not because I needed the features, but because I used it a lot and wanted to say thank you to the devs. Now I'm wondering if it's time to find a new writing app altogether. The version of night mode - now only available in paid - is not the same as it was before, when it was available for free users too. The colours of the document titles are neon levels of bright, a world away from the muted sophicated colour scheme it used to have. The top section of the app where it displays the name of the folder you're in now takes up two lines for no good reason, so there's less room to browse through your files and the whole thing feels cluttered where before it was minimalist. It just doesn't feel as smooth and comfortable to write in as it did before. To look in other recent reviews only to see devs replying to free users who miss night mode to 'get it soon' (it being the paid version) is hardly comforting either. I didn't lose documents, and reconnecting to my Dropbox after the update was fine, no worries there. But I already miss the app this was. Suggestions: - Please make the Night Mode colours light and readable rather than neon bright. - The title header doesn't need to be two lines deep. - Ability to save styles as a custom preset, not just presets and a single unsaved custom. - More fonts and customisability in general, like custom modes for those who find reading with a specific colour filter easier - you could probably tweak Night Vision mode to do just that with a colour palette option. - More font sizes. I like to write on public transport without the people around me reading over my shoulder, would love a smaller font size than 4. - As good as your coding is, your PR skills are a bit less polished. Perhaps consider offering a free trial period of Creative, even if it's just for pre-existing free users? Let people see the worth of your work without holding them to ransom for night mode, please.

This app lost some pretty crucial features in the recent update. Specifically, the ability to whitelist certain apps from tracking was an essential feature; without it, the app is nearly useless for me. (Yes, there's a "pause" feature you can use as a workaround for this missing feature, but it's clunky and forces me to remember yet another thing to do on my phone, which seems counter-productive to the whole point of the app.) The app buckets you into one of several "profiles", presumably because it helps fine-tune the app's parameters to your particular usage habits. It's an interesting idea, but the implementation feels lackluster. As far as I can tell, the only impact these profiles have is that they (1) determine the app's color scheme, and (2) change two default parameters of the app to arbitrary-seeming values that you're probably going to change anyway. The app was also not properly detecting when one day ends and the next begins. I'm not sure if this has been fixed in a recent update, but the app was doing apparently incorrect things that I couldn't understand, which made me trust the whole thing a lot less. I'm waiting to see how future updates improve the app.

I've been using this app for almost a month now, and it's so great! The floating timer is the best feature, by far: I can always see how long I've been actively using any app, which is a real wakeup call. It also doesn't require that every single app is monitored (meaning that you get a notification when you've used it for 30+ minutes), which is useful when you have an app that you don't necessarily use actively, but leave open on your phone. I use Spotify, texting apps, and notetaking apps that way, so I don't care how long I've been "using" the app, because it's open in the foreground all the time. For those of you begging for some way to lock the entire phone or make it tougher to unlock individual apps, that's not what this app is for. It's meant to work together with you and your self control to help you get out of the habit of overusing your phone. If you want an app that blocks individual apps or your entire phone with penalties for trying to unlock them, try Cold Turkey or QualityTime.

Good Simple app, but very useful. Pair it with a Bluetooth keyboard and you can write anywhere, without being distracted by a million buttons and a talking paperclip. Needs a few more features to be a 5 but I love it as it is. I can get my thoughts down alphabetically and quickly. I love this app, but as others have mentioned, an undo button is required! My new favorite app This is so fantastic, I cannot recommend it more for anyone who does any extensive writing from their phone. I do play-by-post rpgs and occasionally like to post from my phone. Good It's greate simple to use and extremely handy. Though could be improved. I write down alot on it and I've noticed that after you go up to 6000 words in starts lagging and stuff. Amazing!!! I write a lot of random things and I also have many stories and I need a place to store them. Best. App. Ever. Worth every second it took to install, and more. I've spent more time using this than any other app. If it hadnt been free I would have still paid. Hollywood Here I Come! I have wanted to find an app like this FOREVER, now I have found it! Stop looking this is the app to get! Decent enough, but could be better. This wordprocessor is easy enough to get to grips with. Some good features, but could do with much more adding to it. Does what it's purported to do Some reviewers kvetch because this isn't a full featured word processor. It's perfect on my Dell Venue 8 tablet and on my Samsung Galaxy S3 phone.

Works great auto saves often. The only thing I might ask for is a way to sync the writings onto my computer or even into Google drive. But it works great for what it promises. A+ It does slow down once there is a decent amount of text in a file, but that doesn't bother me much, i just split what I'm writing into blocks anyway.

Simple app for writing and keeping track of your words. I Couple this with writeometer and I can track my progress and write effectively. Really good so far. Not alot of fuss simple and to the point. Really good app, very simple and practical, the best app for notes I have ever installed, and now the only one I use. from a "serious" writer's prospective I knock out maybe 1000-2000 words a day writing primarily fiction. I've been exploring the various Android word processing options and it's pretty bad out there. If you right a lot there are two main problems I've encountered: 1) You need to have a pretty seamless way of keeping your work backed up somewhere off your tablet. I'm still looking for a silver bullet with this one but in the mean time using the "share to dropbox" option works well, provided you have dropbox installed. Dropbox will handle versioning, accidental deletions or renames, and keeps your files safe in the event that something bad happens to your device(s). 2) You need to have a very responsive word processor that doesn't act goofy. Polaris Office, Kingsoft, and the rest of the office products I've tried (some of them for around $20) really do act goofy. Some have cursor lag, some have the cursor in the "wrong" place, and some display formatting options that you might not want with no way to disable them. The "Writer" app is the best I've found for a real writer. Make the default save option go to dropbox and I'll fall in love.

I was looking for something to help me shut down my phone usage at night, since I wasn't disciplined enough to do it myself. (Put the phone down for bed, then oh! let me check this other thing and down the rabbit hole I'd go.) This app is perfect for that. I can customize each app to be blocked at a specific time, for a set amount of time. It's a little odd in that if I set it to be blocked from 10:30pm - 4:30am, it shows as 2 time chunks: 10:30pm-12am, 12am-4:30am. I had to play around with it a bit before I figured out what was going on. The apps I shut down Sunday night through Thursday night that are my biggest distractions are: all social media, Pinterest, internet, calendar, photos, my list/note taker (Keep), texting, email, news...all while still having the basic functions of my phone accessible in case of emergency. (I do also use do not disturb.) At around 10:15 now, I'm scrambling to squeeze in my last activities for the night. A personal boundary I have no choice but to stick to, yes!! It was also very eye opening to see my daily general phone usage tracked, a feature I wasn't necessarily looking for but thought was interesting. The first day, I was on my phone a total of 4 hours and went into my phone 52 times!! And that was actually less than I would have because I was being somewhat mindful, though forgetting at times, that my usage was being tracked. Overall very cool app, perfect for setting some usage limits I wanted but couldn't follow through with on my own. Good job y'all!! Thank you.

As the developer has noted, they are still working on the compatibility issue with Android 7.0+. On my Android 7.0 phone, the app fails to block settings (i.e., Android system settings). This leaves serious loopholes for one to change time or add users. Admittedly, Android team made any parental app developer miserable by allowing "add another user" too easily available in the status/notification bar (you don't even need to go to settings to do that!). One way to avoid this loophole is to use the phone as a secondary user (who by default cannot add a new user), but running multiple users on Android has too many bugs (external storage access issue, app installation issue). I tried. It's basically not feasible. Another way to avoid the loophole is to install a third-party status/notification bar (e.g., Material Status Bar) to replace Android's default one. But this is sadly defeated by (OFFTIME), because on its "Relax! Your device is at peace" page, the default Android status/notification bar is enforced. I still gave 4-star rating because the app works perfectly otherwise on Android 6.0. I sincerely hope the developer fixes the above loopholes as soon as possible. Many thanks for your great work! Used to be a 5 star app. A recent update broke the app completely, then another a few days later rolled out a "new," version that had scrapped or downgraded most features. The new interface makes it unnecessarily difficult to Flip Off for less than an hour, and the Whitelisted Apps feature is either gone or buried so deep I can't find it. In exchange, there are a bunch of social features--kind of ironic since this app's primary purpose is to get me off social media when I'm supposed to be productive. The text message auto-respond also seems to be gone. I don't see what I'm supposed to use this app for anymore, since I can just turn my phone off for mostly the same effect. If this were a free app, I'd be less annoyed, but I'm a premium subscriber and expect better. EDIT: Flipd has replied to this review. No information has been given on why key features (including those only available to paid subscribers) were removed or why a version that was clearly not ready was shipped. Look at recent reviews. Everyone agrees that some time in mid-August 2017 this went from a really useful app to a broken piece of shovelware. Why this change was made and effectively doubled down on is a mystery, and Flipd isn't talking. I wouldn't recommend giving a developer like this your money. EDIT 2: Full lock is back, whitelisted apps are still not, so there's no real upgrade over just turning your phone off. The "updated" interface that makes it difficult to Flip Off for any amount of time that isn't exactly 1 hour hasn't been improved. The paid version of this app is *still* worse than the free version used to be. Perplexing, since the devs have clearly been working on the app *and* keep piping in to remind me that the app is still ruined. My yearly subscription expires in February, so I'm gonna keep one eye on this app until then, but the devs continued deafness to app usability is hard to ignore. Still would not recommend. EDIT3: The White List is back, but only in name. The option is simply to enable or disable it. I can find no way to set what apps are Whitelisted, nor how to even tell what's on the Whitelist--I assume it's a handful of default apps like Play Music, which I don't use. Plus I have no way of knowing if that guess is right. The interface is *still* a form-over-function mess that looks pretty but makes flipping off for any amount of time that isn't exactly one hour needlessly difficult. I'm starting to feel sorry for the lady who has to reply to all these negative reviews as the actual development team continues to be utterly tone deaf about why people use this app.

For anyone trying to find an app that actually works to block apps in an effective way on Android, this is a must read. This is an absolutely incredible app. Absolute credit to the developers, great work guys. I've only given it 1 star to catch the attention of developers for the few things if added would genuinely make this app a 5 star app. I've tried; stay focused, freedom.to, cold turkey (both online and on the phone app), FocusON, Smart Lock, AppBlock - Stay Focused and Offtime (the app I'm currently using). Below is Pros & Cons... ~~~~~PROS~~~~ - very few apps I have tried if not any actually block the apps, this does... - You can toggle between a definite inability to access until the timer runs out or re-open the apps after restarting your phone depending on your will-power. - this was the biggest for me... You can run different app blocking groups simultaneously without them blocking out. Super convenient. - schedule days that the selected blocked apps can turn on & off - even as easy as when setting up a group or apps to block you don't need to set a schedule but can just set a (x amount of time from now) option which is so much more convenient then all of the other apps I had tried. - there's these little productivity quotes or pick me ups that pop up every time you try and access the app thats blocked. It's a happy medium between super corny quote and blank page instead of the app opening up. Most app blocking apps are either doing one extreme or the other. ~~~ CONS ~~~ - doesn't have the ability to 'log in' or sync across multiple devices, often the apps I block on my phone are the apps I want to block on my tablet too. Saves others having to set up and de select 20-30 apps every device. - allowing the app to be a device administrator, because at the end of it all if I uninstall the app, it bypasses everything. It can be uninstalled easily and then due to the lack of sync options / can't be backed up & restored. It isn't possible. - a desktop app through website or download... If these would be adjusted would happily make it a 5 star rating & would happily pay for this. Other programs are charging up to $6 while doing 80% of everything but 100% of nothing. You most certainly could get away with charging a good 4.50/5 with all of these features included. Again, absolutely incredible work guys. Look forward to the updates.

It takes usually a minute to restore the session and within this time the app can be deleted and reinstalled again. I suggest the following: either allow the app to prevent from rebooting the phone or have the app instantly recover the previous session right after the phone restarts. Great, useful, and ugly RescueTime measures your computer use across multiple devices to help you identify time sinks and improve your own efficiency. It is not a project management or billing tool, although it can be a very useful contributor to one. Because it runs on Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, Chrome and Firefox (no iOS), I can see how much time I wasted while browsing the web at my desk, reading ebooks on the toilet, and playing some dumb game during my commute. It's relatively seamless, and pretty much just works. It falls down on manual time tracking, offering only an on-off toggle for 6 presets (and a write-in field), and integrates easily with only two other services -- for everything else the company will point you to their API. It cries out for a project tool, and better manual time-reporting and tweaking. The reporting could use improvement in spots, but it's still pretty good out of the box. The Android version does not have "Focus mode", for technical reasons. If you need it, the RescueTime platform is both useful and helpful, and I have found no other tool that offers the fully automated usage tracking across as many platforms.
